# Mehul Jatania
## Chief Financial Office
Mehul Jatania is the Chief Financial Officer at Vastu Housing Finance, with over two decades of experience across financial services, strategy, and business building. He has a strong track record across the full business and investment lifecycle, including the creation and scaling of lending platforms, driving digital transformation, and executing complex strategic initiatives.
Prior to joining Vastu Housing Finance, Mehul spent nearly a decade with the Centrum Group, where he joined as SVP – Strategy and later served as the Chief Financial Officer of Centrum Housing Finance Limited. He played a pivotal role in scaling the housing finance franchise, raising equity and debt, executing acquisitions, and strengthening funding partnerships.
 ... 
# Satish Nair
## Chief Business Officer
Satish Nair is the Chief Business Officer at Vastu Housing Finance. He leads business, portfolio and product management, and as part of the leadership group engages with investors, regulators, financial institutions, market participants and development financial institutions (DFI). Previously, he was managing treasury, marketing, corporate affairs and regulatory relationships at Vastu.
Prior to joining Vastu, he has led across various functions in rating products, business development, fixed income and industry research, investor relations, regulatory reporting, credit policy, and compliance at Fitch Ratings, India Ratings and Research and Brickwork Ratings.
Satish is a management and accounting graduate from the University of Mumbai.
 ... 
# Vikki Soni
## Head of Finance & Accounts
Vikki is a founding team member at Vastu. He in his previous role spearheaded the Finance team at L&T Housing Finance Limited and was responsible for managing the overall F&A function. He is a seasoned finance professional with strong technical skills and excellent operational experience. He brings with him rich expertise in Finance & Accounts, Taxation, Regulatory and Statutory Compliance, Investor Relations, Internal Audit, Treasury Management and Business Strategy. Vikki heads Finance & Accounts and Compliance functions at Vastu.
Vikki is a Chartered Accountant by Qualification with 8 years of Post Qualification experience.

excerpts:
The earnings profile for Va stu Housing has been supported by healthy margins and low credit costs. Cost of funds has remained competitive with Rs 1,925 crore raised in fiscal 2023 at ~8.5% on a weighted average basis due to diversified funding profile across instruments and investor s. As a result, the company reported healthy profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 274 crore (including a gain on assignment transactions of Rs 80 crore) with return on managed assets (RoMA) of 5.0% during fiscal 2023, against Rs 176 crore, Rs 67 crore and 4.8%, re spectively, in fiscal 2022. It further reported PAT of Rs 66 crore with annualised RoMA of 3.9% in the first quarter of fiscal 2024.
Going ahead, Vastu Housing’s ability to continue to profitably scale up operations while managing asset quality, further augmenting the company’s market position, will be a key rating sensitivity factor. |
| --- | |
| |
||Analytical Approach
 ... 
Multiples Alternate Asset Management, after the recent capital raise, remains the largest shareholder with ~70% stake on a diluted basis in Vastu Housi ng as on March 31, 2023 (94.13% as on March 31, 2021).
Consequent to the capital raise and supported by healthy internal accrual, the company’s networth increased to Rs 2,467 crore as on June 30, 2023 from Rs 2,106 crore as on March 31, 2021. As a result , adjusted gearing also improved to 1.6 times as of June 2023 from 1.8 times as of March 2021. However, with scale-up of operations, gearing is expected to increase gradually over the next few years. On a steady-state basis, the company is likely to mainta in gearing of 5-6 times at a consolidated level.
Vastu Housing has infused Rs 300 crore in its subsidiary, Vastu Finserve, out of which Rs 175 crore was infused in fiscal 2023.
Strong risk management systems, with emphasis on technology-driven processe s, resulting in stable asset quality
 ... 
While the company remains a small player in the overall mortgage finance indu stry, Vastu Housing remains a profitable and sizeable player in the pure-play affordable housing industry. The average monthly disbursement for the company in fiscal 2024 was ~Rs 240 crore as of June 2023 on a standalone basis and ~Rs 360 crore on a consol idated basis. Disbursements over the last 24 months form a large proportion of AUM for affordable housing financiers, this being at 84% of its AUM as on March 31, 2023 for Vastu.
In the housing business, the management has forayed into the micro-housing a nd MSME segment, building its digital sourcing capability and investing further in the technology platform.

# ADB, Vastu Housing Finance to Enhance Access to Affordable and Sustainable Housing in India
## News from Country Offices | 23 December 2024
### SHARE THIS PAGE
NEW DELHI, INDIA (23 December 2024) – The Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Vastu Housing Finance Corporation Limited (Vastu) have entered into a senior secured loan agreement of up to $70 million to enhance access to affordable and sustainable housing loans in India’s underserved states. This financing will be utilized to provide loans to economically weaker sections and low-income groups, with an emphasis on female borrowers. At least 15% of the funds will be allocated to first-time borrowers.
"ADB aims to address the critical housing shortage in India while promoting environmentally friendly housing that enhances climate resilience for homeowners by focusing on lower-income households and sustainable housing," said PSOD Director General Suzanne Gaboury. "This partnership with Vastu illustrates ADB's commitment to supporting financial inclusion and sustainable development in India, in alignment with the country’s national financial inclusion strategy."
According to the Reserve Bank of India, shortfalls of 45 million houses for economically weaker communities and 50 million for low-income groups account for 95% of India’s overall housing deficit. These groups often struggle to access credit due to high mortgage costs and limited credit history. This highlights the necessity for affordable housing finance companies that provide loans to new borrowers and self-employed individuals in rural and semi-urban areas.
Sandeep Menon, Founder, MD & CEO, Vastu, said, "Vastu is poised to expand our reach and deepen our impact in extending affordable housing finance to the credit-underserved segments, with a focus on women borrowers. We are glad to partner with ADB to further this vision. Together, we aim to bridge the credit gap for India’s emerging middle-class and lower-income households.”
